backlog.spec: Replace the bit-vector Morgan fingerprint with a count fingerprint: use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same radius-2 generator folded to 2048 bins. Keep the RandomForestRegressor settings unchanged. Repeated substructures then contribute their multiplicity, which carries size and functional-group information the bit vector loses.
backlog.title: Morgan count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute all RDKit descriptors with Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, and clip values to [-1e6, 1e6]. Concatenate this block with the Morgan count fingerprint and fit the same random forest. Physicochemical descriptors such as TPSA, MolWt and logP are known drivers of Caco-2 permeability that bit fingerprints capture only indirectly.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D descriptor block

backlog.spec: Build a compact set of about 14 interpretable features: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, formal charge sum, and counts of carboxylic acids, basic amines and quaternary or permanently charged nitrogens. Append these to the Morgan counts. Dense, mechanistically meaningful features may help a tree model generalise across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Hand-picked permeability descriptor core

backlog.spec: Replace Morgan with the 167-bit MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) as the only molecular representation. Keep the random forest settings. MACCS encodes general functional-group presence and is a smaller, less sparse representation that may generalise better across scaffolds.
backlog.title: MACCS keys as the fingerprint

backlog.spec: Replace Morgan with hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Keep the random forest unchanged. Atom pairs encode topological distance between atoms and capture overall molecular shape and size differently from circular environments.
backlog.title: Atom-pair count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Build the feature vector by concatenating hashed topological-torsion count fingerprints (1024 bins) with Morgan count fingerprints (1024 bins). Use the same random forest. Torsion features describe local conformational paths, which are relevant to membrane permeation.
backlog.title: Topological torsion plus Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Use the Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator set to the feature-invariant generator (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) to produce pharmacophore-style count fingerprints at radius 2 with 2048 bins. Keep the random forest unchanged. Feature invariants group atoms into donors, acceptors and aromatic classes, which can generalise better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP-like)

backlog.spec: After fitting the random forest, collect the predictions of every individual tree for the test molecules and return their per-molecule median instead of the mean. The metric is MAE, and the median of tree predictions is the conditional median estimate, which is more robust to skewed leaf distributions. No change to training is needed.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees prediction

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor using 500 trees, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=-1 and random_state=seed. Keep the Morgan count features. Extra-randomised splits add variance reduction that often helps on small, noisy regression sets.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees instead of random forest

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM (LGBMRegressor) on Morgan counts concatenated with RDKit descriptors, using objective='l1' so the fitted function targets the same absolute error as the metric. Use num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.03, 600 rounds, feature_fraction=0.5, bagging_fraction=0.8 with bagging_freq=1, and random_state=seed.
backlog.title: LightGBM with L1 objective

backlog.spec: Train CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE' on Morgan counts concatenated with RDKit descriptors. Use depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, 800 iterations, random_seed=seed and verbose=0. Ordered boosting in CatBoost is well suited to small datasets and reduces overfitting.
backlog.title: CatBoost with MAE loss

backlog.spec: Train XGBRegressor with objective='reg:absoluteerror' on Morgan counts concatenated with RDKit descriptors. Use max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, 600 estimators, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed and tree_method='hist'. Shallow trees with an L1 objective keep predictions robust to outlier permeability values.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 90/10 groups by Murcko scaffold, using a deterministic shuffle seeded by seed. Train a LightGBM L1 model with up to 2000 rounds on the 90% part and record the validation MAE curve. Refit on all training data using the best round count scaled by 1.1. This learning-rate schedule chooses the number of boosting rounds without leaking scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-held-out early stopping for boosting

backlog.spec: Train a LightGBM L1 model where the learning rate decays geometrically over rounds: use a learning_rate_schedule callback that multiplies the rate by 0.995 each round starting from 0.1, for 800 rounds total. Use Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors. The decaying step size reduces late-round overfitting on a small training set.
backlog.title: Staged learning-rate decay for boosting

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints (intersection over union of bit sets) for train-train and test-train pairs, and fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed', C=10 and epsilon=0.1. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecules and often beat RBF kernels on fingerprints.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR

backlog.spec: Build the Tanimoto kernel matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints, as for train-train and test-train pairs. Fit KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed'. Choose alpha from {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by an inner 5-fold grouped CV on the training data, grouping by Murcko scaffold, and refit on all training data with the best alpha.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kernel ridge with tuned regularisation

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarities between test and training molecules on binary Morgan fingerprints. Predict each test molecule as the weighted mean of the k=10 most similar training molecules, with weights equal to similarity cubed. Nearest-neighbour averaging is a strong local baseline for congeneric series.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-weighted nearest neighbours

backlog.spec: Standardise the RDKit descriptor block (fit scaler on training data, clip extreme z-scores to ±5). Train sklearn MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,128), alpha=1e-2 as L2 weight decay, learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=500 and random_state=seed. Standardisation is needed so the network trains stably on descriptors with very different scales.
backlog.title: Standardised descriptors into a regularised MLP

backlog.spec: Combine Morgan counts with standardised RDKit descriptors, then remove columns that are constant in training. Fit ElasticNetCV with l1_ratio in {0.1, 0.5, 0.9} and 5-fold CV for alpha, using the same seed for the folds. The linear model provides a different inductive bias that may ensemble well with tree models.
backlog.title: ElasticNet on sparse fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Before fitting any model, clip the training target values to their 2nd and 98th percentiles computed on train_y only. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged (for example, the random forest on Morgan counts). Extreme measured values in a small noisy dataset distort squared-error fits, and clipping reduces their influence.
backlog.title: Winsorise training targets

backlog.spec: Fit an ordinary least squares model on training data using TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP as inputs. Compute residuals train_y minus the linear prediction, fit the random forest on Morgan counts to these residuals, and add the linear prediction back for test molecules. A physicochemical baseline lets the forest model only what the simple trend misses.
backlog.title: Linear-baseline residual target

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a small grid over RandomForestRegressor max_features in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and min_samples_leaf in {1, 3, 5}, scored with an inner GroupKFold (3 folds) where groups are Murcko scaffolds of the training molecules. Use 100 trees during the search, pick the best MAE, then refit with 300 trees on all training data. Selecting hyperparameters under scaffold-grouped validation matches the test protocol.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped tuning of forest hyperparameters

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, produce out-of-fold predictions on training data (inner 5-fold, grouped by Murcko scaffold) from three base models: random forest on Morgan counts, LightGBM L1 on counts plus descriptors, and Tanimoto-kernel SVR. Find nonnegative blending weights summing to one that minimise the mean absolute error of the out-of-fold predictions, using scipy.optimize.minimize. Refit base models on all training data and blend their test predictions.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with nonnegative MAE weights

backlog.spec: Average the test predictions of three independently fitted models with equal weights: random forest on Morgan counts, LightGBM L1 on counts plus descriptors, and Tanimoto-kernel SVR on binary Morgan. Each model is trained on all training data with the same seed. Averaging diverse model families usually reduces variance without any tuning.
backlog.title: Equal-weight three-model average

backlog.spec: Train 10 random forests of 100 trees each, where each forest is fit on a bootstrap-free random subsample of 70% of the training molecules drawn with a seed-derived RNG. Average all 10 forests' predictions for the test molecules. Subsample bagging decorrelates the component models and smooths the final prediction.
backlog.title: Bagged random forests over subsamples

backlog.spec: Train five LightGBM L1 models on Morgan counts plus descriptors, with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4, using bagging_fraction=0.7, feature_fraction=0.5 and subsample rows per tree. Return the mean of the five predictions. Averaging stochastic boosted models reduces the variance introduced by row and column subsampling.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged stochastic boosting

backlog.spec: Train sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor with loss='quantile' and alpha=0.5 on Morgan counts concatenated with RDKit descriptors, using n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=3, subsample=0.8 and random_state=seed. A median regression objective directly targets the absolute-error criterion used to score the model.
backlog.title: Quantile (median) gradient boosting

backlog.spec: After any model produces test predictions, clip them to the closed interval [min(train_y), max(train_y)] computed on training data only. Keep the random forest on Morgan counts otherwise unchanged. Clipping prevents extrapolation to implausible permeability values for molecules far from the training distribution.
backlog.title: Clip predictions to training target range

backlog.spec: Before fitting the random forest, drop Morgan bit columns that are set in fewer than 3 or more than 97 percent of training molecules. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Removing near-constant bits reduces noise in split selection, so the max_features subsampling is spent on informative features.
backlog.title: Variance-threshold feature pruning

backlog.spec: Compute a 30-component PCA on standardised RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts, fit on the training molecules only, and append the component scores to the feature matrix for LightGBM L1. The compressed dense representation gives trees smooth axes that raw sparse bits do not provide.
backlog.title: PCA embedding features for boosting

backlog.spec: Keep the current MACCS-plus-descriptor features and the CatBoost MAE model. Add rsm=0.3 (random subspace per split), bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' with subsample=0.7, and l2_leaf_reg=10. Leave ITERS and LR unchanged. The aim is to reduce overfitting to shared scaffolds by decorrelating trees.
backlog.title: CatBoost with strong column and row subsampling

backlog.spec: Train one CatBoost MAE model with ITERS=800 as now. Instead of taking only the final prediction, call model.staged_predict(test_X) and average the predictions from iterations 300, 400, ..., 800. This costs no extra training and smooths the late-stage overfit to training scaffolds. Keep the seed argument as the only source of randomness.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging along the boosting path

backlog.spec: Replace loss_function='MAE' with loss_function='Huber:delta=0.5' and set leaf_estimation_method='Newton' in CatBoostRegressor. Keep depth, LR and ITERS. Evaluate the official loss as normal. The Huber loss keeps MAE-like robustness to outliers in the Caco-2 labels while giving smoother gradients for the leaf fits.
backlog.title: Huber loss with Newton leaf estimation

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a logistic classifier (sklearn, default regularization) on binary Morgan bits to separate train molecules from test molecules. Convert its probabilities to weights p/(1-p), clip them to [0.2, 5], and normalise to mean 1. Pass these as sample_weight to CatBoost. This is a covariate-shift correction that emphasises training molecules resembling the unseen test skeletons.
backlog.title: Density-ratio importance weighting toward test chemistry

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute binary Morgan radius-2 fingerprints for train and test. Using an inner 5-fold split of the training set, compute for each training molecule the mean target of its k=5 most Tanimoto-similar molecules in the other folds, and for each test molecule the mean target of its 5 nearest training molecules. Append these two values as a single extra column to the MACCS-plus-descriptor matrix and fit CatBoost as now. The inner folds prevent leakage of a molecule's own label.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold Tanimoto nearest-neighbour feature for boosting

backlog.spec: Fit CatBoost on the training set as now and predict the test molecules. Append the test molecules with these predicted values as pseudo-labels to the training set, using sample_weight=0.5 for them, and refit a fresh CatBoost with the same seed. Return the second-round predictions for the test molecules. This transductive step lets the model adapt its splits to the chemistry of the unseen molecules.
backlog.title: Pseudo-labelling with test-set predictions

backlog.spec: Keep the current features and CatBoost MAE model. Locate the RDKit descriptor columns for TPSA, NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors (by name, using the order of Descriptors.descList). Pass monotone_constraints to CatBoostRegressor with -1 for each of these columns (higher polarity lowers permeability) and 0 elsewhere. The constraint restricts the trees from learning spurious polarity trends that would not transfer to new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on polarity descriptors

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, group training molecules by Murcko scaffold. Draw 6 bootstrap models: each takes a random 80% of the unique scaffolds (with the seed-derived RNG), keeps all their molecules, and fits a CatBoost MAE model with fewer ITERS (500). Average the 6 predictions on the test molecules. Scaffold-level subsampling makes each bag see a different set of skeletons, which is the main source of generalisation error here.
backlog.title: Scaffold-subsampled bagging of CatBoost

backlog.spec: Before fitting, map the training targets to a standard normal by rank: r = rankdata(y)/(n+1), z = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(r). Fit CatBoost MAE on z. Transform predictions back to the original scale by applying np.interp from the sorted z-values of the training set to the sorted original targets, with linear extrapolation clipped to the training range. This stabilises the heavy tails of the permeability distribution before boosting.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank target transform with inverse mapping

backlog.spec: Inside featurize, for each molecule add a conformer with AllChem.EmbedMolecule(mol, randomSeed=0) and, if it succeeds, compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcPMI1, CalcPMI2, CalcPMI3, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2 and CalcRadiusOfGyration; use zeros when embedding fails. Append these 7 values to the existing MACCS-plus-descriptor vector and fit CatBoost as now. Shape and planarity are physically relevant to membrane transport and are not captured by 2D features.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from an ETKDG conformer

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the np.linalg.lstsq OLS prior on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP with a least-absolute-deviation linear fit: sklearn.linear_model.QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=0.0, solver='highs') on the standardised four base features, fit on training molecules only. Keep the CatBoost MAE model unchanged and fit it on y minus the L1 prior's training predictions. Test prediction is CatBoost output plus the L1 prior's test prediction. This reduces outlier sensitivity of the prior, which the MAE objective is meant to handle.
backlog.title: Median (L1) linear prior instead of OLS

backlog.spec: Compute four RDKit SMARTS counts per molecule: carboxylic acids, tetrazoles or acyl sulfonamides (acidic), aliphatic amines that are not amides or anilines (basic), permanently charged nitrogen, and phenols. Append these counts to the four base descriptors in the OLS prior matrices A_tr and A_te only. Leave the CatBoost feature matrix unchanged. The goal is a logD-like linear baseline, since permeability depends on ionisation at pH 7.4, without adding inputs to CatBoost.
backlog.title: Ionisation-class counts in the linear prior only

backlog.spec: For each molecule collect hashed Morgan radius-1 and radius-2 environment IDs. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 5-fold KFold on the training set to build out-of-fold target encodings: for each environment ID, the mean OLS residual of training molecules containing it, shrunk toward zero with about 5 pseudo-observations. A molecule's encoding is the mean of its environments' shrunk means. Fit a ridge regression from these encodings to the OLS residuals with alpha picked from 3 values by inner CV. Add its prediction to the OLS prior, then fit the CatBoost MAE model on what remains. Test-time encodings use all training molecules.
backlog.title: Smoothed out-of-fold substructure target encoding as a second prior

backlog.spec: Stage 1: fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the OLS-residual target using an inner 4-fold KFold over the training set to produce out-of-fold predictions. Stage 2: compute the out-of-fold residuals and fit a second, shallower CatBoost MAE model (depth 4, 300 iterations, lr 0.03) on the Morgan-plus-descriptor features to predict those residuals. At test time, sum the full-data stage 1 prediction, the stage 2 prediction, and the OLS prior. Reduce stage 1 iterations if needed to stay under the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Two-stage residual boosting with inner out-of-fold residuals

backlog.spec: Split the training molecules at the median TPSA into two groups. Fit a separate CatBoost MAE model on the OLS-residual target for each group, using the same features and settings. At test time, route each test molecule to the expert for its TPSA side, using the training median as the cut. Add the OLS prior back to both predictions. The aim is to let the boosting specialise on low-polarity molecules, which are dominated by passive diffusion, separately from high-polarity ones.
backlog.title: Regime mixture of experts split on polarity

backlog.spec: Keep loss_function='MAE' and the existing residual setup, and change only the leaf estimation: pass leaf_estimation_method='Exact' (or 'Newton' if Exact is unsupported with the chosen loss) and leaf_estimation_iterations=10. Also try l2_leaf_reg=5 in the same run. This changes how each leaf value is optimised under the absolute-error objective. Compare against the incumbent with the same seeds and folds.
backlog.title: Newton or exact leaf estimation for the MAE CatBoost

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of every training molecule in fit_predict. Give each molecule a sample weight of 1 divided by the square root of its scaffold's count within the training set, then rescale the weights to mean 1. Pass them as sample_weight to CatBoostRegressor.fit. Large scaffold series then do not dominate the boosting loss, which should help generalisation to unseen skeletons that the harness tests on.
backlog.title: Scaffold-balanced sample weights

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run an inner 4-fold GroupKFold over Murcko scaffolds to obtain out-of-fold CatBoost MAE predictions on the training set (residual target, OLS prior added back). Fit sklearn.isotonic.IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip') mapping these out-of-fold predictions to the true training targets, minimising squared error. Fit the final CatBoost on all training data and apply the isotonic map to its test predictions. This corrects systematic shrinkage of boosted predictions toward the middle of the range.
backlog.title: Isotonic recalibration of inner out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: After the CatBoost MAE model is fit on the OLS-residual target, compute the training residuals on the training set as out-of-fold predictions from an inner 4-fold GroupKFold. For each test molecule, find its k=5 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on binary Morgan radius-2 fingerprints. Add to the test prediction a similarity-weighted average of those neighbours' out-of-fold residuals, shrunk by a factor of 0.5, and skip the correction when the maximum similarity is below 0.3. Only the test-time correction changes; the boosting model is unchanged.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-neighbour residual correction after boosting

backlog.spec: Before fitting CatBoost, duplicate the training set twice with the same feature rows but targets (y minus OLS prior) jittered by independent Gaussian noise with sd 0.1 in log units, seeded from the seed argument. Concatenate the original and the two jittered copies and fit the CatBoost MAE model on the 3x data. The noise acts as a smoothness prior on the target and should reduce overfitting to individual noisy measurements. Keep iterations the same and check the runtime, which will be about 3x.
backlog.title: Target-noise augmentation as a regulariser

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP and the Morgan-plus-descriptor features. Fit a first CatBoost on the OLS residual with loss_function='Huber:delta=0.3' for about 400 iterations, then fit a second CatBoost with loss MAE on the residual left after the first model's in-sample predictions, using the same learning rate and depth. Final prediction = OLS + Huber model + MAE model. Use the seed for both models. This anneals the loss from smooth to median-seeking.
backlog.title: Huber-then-MAE two-phase boosting

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS residual CatBoost pipeline. Before fitting, create an equal number of synthetic training rows by drawing random pairs of training molecules (seeded), sampling lambda from Beta(0.4, 0.4) per pair, and forming convex combinations of their feature vectors and of their OLS residual targets. Stack real and synthetic rows and fit CatBoost MAE once. Test features are unchanged. This is a mixup-style regulariser that smooths the decision surface between neighbouring chemotypes.
backlog.title: Feature-space mixup augmentation

backlog.spec: In featurize and base_features, standardise each SMILES first: parse, keep the largest covalent fragment (rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or split on '.' and keep the heaviest piece), then neutralise charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Fall back to the raw molecule if parsing or standardisation fails. Compute all fingerprints and descriptors on the cleaned molecule. Everything else, including the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE, stays the same.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurisation

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit the OLS prior and a quick CatBoost MAE (300 iterations) on the training set with 4-fold inner KFold (shuffled, seeded). Compute out-of-fold absolute residuals. Drop the 5 percent of training rows with the largest residuals, then refit the full pipeline (OLS on the kept rows, CatBoost MAE with the standard settings) and predict the test set. This removes likely label-noise molecules rather than clipping their targets.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold residual trimming of training rows

backlog.spec: Replace the OLS prior with a ridge model on random Fourier features: standardise the RDKit descriptors using training statistics only, drop constant columns, and apply sklearn.kernel_approximation.Nystroem (RBF, gamma set to 1/n_features, n_components=300, random_state=seed) followed by Ridge(alpha=10). Fit it on the training fold, subtract its in-sample predictions from train_y to form the residual, and fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on that residual. Add the ridge predictions back at test time.
backlog.title: Nystroem RBF kernel prior in place of OLS

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE on its residual. Inside fit_predict, run an inner 4-fold scaffold-grouped split (GroupKFold on Murcko scaffold strings, seeded) on the training fold to get out-of-fold CatBoost residual predictions. Choose a shrink factor alpha from {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2} that minimises the out-of-fold MAE of OLS + alpha times the CatBoost residual. Then fit CatBoost on all training rows and return OLS + alpha times its test residual prediction.
backlog.title: Post-hoc shrinkage of the boosted residual

backlog.spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with a richer linear prior: natural cubic spline basis (sklearn SplineTransformer, 4 knots, degree 3) on TPSA, MolLogP and MolWt, plus NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors as linear terms. Fit it with Ridge(alpha=1.0) on the training fold. Keep the CatBoost MAE model on the residual exactly as in the current script. The aim is a better nonlinear baseline that CatBoost has less need to rediscover.
backlog.title: Spline-basis linear prior

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the residual target. Train six CatBoost MAE models: depths 4, 6 and 8, each with two seeds derived from the seed argument (seed and seed+1000). Use 800 iterations at lr 0.05 for depth 6, and scale iterations to 1000 for depth 4 and 600 for depth 8. Return the element-wise median of the six residual predictions plus the OLS term. Median combining suits the MAE objective.
backlog.title: Depth-diverse CatBoost bag with median aggregation

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model. Change the CatBoost settings for a small dataset of about 600 training rows: boosting_type='Ordered', l2_leaf_reg=10, min_data_in_leaf=5 (only valid with Depthwise or Lossguide grow policy, so set grow_policy='Depthwise' too), and keep depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations. Ordered boosting reduces target leakage on small data. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Ordered boosting with strong leaf regularisation

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the residual CatBoost MAE model. Stage 1: rank training rows by the absolute OLS residual and fit CatBoost MAE (400 iterations, lr 0.05) on the easiest 70 percent. Stage 2: continue training that model on all rows with init_model=stage1 and 400 further iterations, so the hard, noisy molecules enter after the model has learned the bulk structure. Return the stage-2 prediction on the test set plus the OLS term.
backlog.title: Curriculum boosting from easy to hard molecules

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after computing the Morgan count matrix for the training fold, compute the absolute Spearman correlation between each bit and the OLS residual y - A_tr @ coef, using only training molecules. Keep the 256 bits with the highest correlation (ignore bits that are constant in the training fold) and append them to the RDKit descriptor block. Use only training-fold statistics so no test information leaks. Leave the OLS prior, CatBoost MAE settings and seed handling unchanged.
backlog.title: Supervised fingerprint-bit selection on the residual

backlog.spec: Fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the OLS residual with all features, then read model.get_feature_importance(). Keep the top 300 features by importance (the fingerprint and descriptor columns together) and refit a fresh CatBoost MAE model with the same settings on that reduced matrix. Selection uses only the training fold, and the second fit uses the same seed. Predict as before by adding the OLS prior back.
backlog.title: Two-pass CatBoost feature pruning by importance

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan count vector by counts divided by the number of heavy atoms of each molecule, and append log(heavy atom count) as one extra column. This turns raw substructure counts into per-atom densities so large and small molecules are comparable, while keeping the size information the density loses. Keep the RDKit descriptor block, the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE model unchanged.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-normalised count fingerprint with size channel

backlog.spec: Build count fingerprints at radii 1 and 3 in addition to the existing radius 2, each hashed to 1024 bits. On the training fold only, drop any bit that is nonzero in fewer than 3 training molecules, and keep the rest. Concatenate the three blocks with the RDKit descriptors and feed them to the same OLS-prior plus CatBoost MAE pipeline. The change is the radius and frequency filter only.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Morgan counts with frequency filter

backlog.spec: For a set of about 10 RDKit descriptors (for example TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumRotatableBonds, RingCount, FractionCSP3, NumAromaticRings, HeavyAtomCount, NumHAcceptors, BertzCT), fit a Ridge regression from the Morgan count fingerprint to each descriptor. Produce these predictions for the training molecules with an inner 5-fold split grouped by Murcko scaffold, so that training rows never see their own target. For test molecules, use a ridge fit on the full training fold. Append the predicted descriptor values as features to CatBoost. This is an auxiliary-target embedding, not a stacking of final predictions.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold ridge predictions of RDKit descriptors as features

backlog.spec: Replace the single global OLS prior with a locally weighted linear fit per query. For each test molecule, find its k=100 nearest training molecules in the standardised space of the four base features (TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, MolLogP), weight them with a Gaussian kernel of their distance, and solve a weighted least-squares fit of y on those four features plus intercept to get that molecule's prior. For training rows, use the same procedure with the row itself excluded. Then fit CatBoost MAE on y minus this local prior and add the local prior back at prediction time.
backlog.title: Locally weighted linear prior instead of global OLS

backlog.spec: Estimate the density of the training targets with a Gaussian kernel density estimate (Scott bandwidth) computed on train_y within the training fold. Give each training molecule a sample weight equal to the inverse density, normalised to mean 1 and clipped to the range [0.2, 5]. Pass these weights to CatBoostRegressor.fit when fitting the MAE model on the OLS residual. This pushes capacity toward rare target values, the tails where MAE errors accumulate, and leaves the features and prior unchanged.
backlog.title: Label-density reweighting of training targets

backlog.spec: Train 6 CatBoost MAE models on the OLS residual, each with depth 5, 300 iterations and learning rate 0.1. Give each model a random 40 percent of the feature columns, drawn with a seed-derived RNG, and use row subsampling of 0.8. Average their test predictions, then add the OLS prior. This is a random-subspace bagging ensemble. It is different from the single model with rsm, which was already tried, because each member sees a different feature subset.
backlog.title: Random-subspace ensemble of small CatBoost MAE models

backlog.spec: Split the training fold into 5 bins by quantile of the OLS residual. Train 5 CatBoost MAE models, each on a bootstrap that draws the same fraction of rows from every bin (stratified bagging), using a different seed. Average their test predictions and add the OLS prior back. Stratification keeps the tails of the residual distribution represented in every bag, which ordinary random bootstrap can drop. Keep depth, learning rate and iterations at the current values.
backlog.title: Stratified target-bin bagging of CatBoost

backlog.spec: Instead of one OLS prior on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, fit three OLS priors: the current four features, the two features TPSA and MolLogP only, and an intercept-only prior. Average their predictions on training and test rows with equal weights to form the prior. Then fit the CatBoost MAE model on y minus this averaged prior, as in the current pipeline. The aim is a less brittle baseline, because the prior sets the scale of the residual the boosting learns.
backlog.title: Averaged linear priors of several feature subsets

backlog.spec: Replace the single CatBoost MAE regressor with an ordinal decomposition. Choose K=9 thresholds at the 10th to 90th percentiles of the training target (after subtracting the OLS prior). For each threshold t_k, fit a CatBoostClassifier (Logloss, same depth/lr, 300 to 400 iterations, seed) on the features to predict 1[residual > t_k]. For each test molecule, estimate its conditional CDF at each threshold from the predicted probabilities, enforce monotonicity by a running max over k, and return the median by linear interpolation of the CDF across the threshold grid, plus the OLS prior. The output is the conditional median, which is the target of MAE, but it is estimated distributionally.
backlog.title: Ordinal CDF median via threshold classifiers

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE model on the residual. After fitting, obtain leaf indices for all training and test molecules with model.calc_leaf_indexes (or apply). For each test molecule, form weights over training molecules equal to the number of trees in which the two share a leaf, divided by the leaf size per tree (the quantile-regression-forest weighting). Return the weighted median of the training residuals under those weights, plus the OLS prior, in place of the model's direct prediction. Blend 50/50 with the direct prediction to limit variance.
backlog.title: Conditional median from CatBoost leaf co-membership

backlog.spec: Before fitting, replace each training target by a smoothed value: y_tilde_i = (1 - lam) * y_i + lam * mean of y_j over the k=5 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules j != i (binary Morgan radius 2), with lam=0.3. Neighbours are found within the training fold only. Fit the existing OLS prior and CatBoost MAE model on y_tilde, and predict test molecules as usual. This shrinks label noise toward local chemistry without touching the features or the model class.
backlog.title: kNN target smoothing as regularisation

backlog.spec: Before any featurisation, canonicalise every SMILES: parse with RDKit, call Chem.RemoveStereochemistry on each molecule, then apply rdMolStandardize.TautomerEnumerator().Canonicalize with a fixed max tautomer count, falling back to the original molecule if canonicalisation raises an exception. Compute Morgan bits, RDKit descriptors, and the OLS prior features from the canonical molecules. Keep everything else unchanged so the only difference is the canonical input.
backlog.title: Stereo and tautomer canonicalisation before featurisation

backlog.spec: Fit sklearn PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson', standardize=True) on the RDKit descriptor block of the training fold only, apply it to training and test descriptors, and clip the transformed values to plus or minus 6 standard deviations. Concatenate the transformed descriptors with the existing binary MACCS-free Morgan bits (or the current feature set). The OLS prior and CatBoost stay unchanged. The aim is to tame heavy-tailed size and count descriptors that split badly for trees in a fixed-depth model.
backlog.title: Yeo-Johnson transform of descriptor inputs

backlog.spec: Build the fingerprint vocabulary jointly from train and test SMILES (unsupervised, no labels). Count how often each hashed Morgan radius-2 bit (2048 bits) occurs across all molecules in train plus test. Keep only bits present in at least 3 molecules and at least 1 molecule on both sides of the split, so features are non-degenerate for the test set. Drop the others from both matrices before fitting. Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE model unchanged. This adapts the feature space to the unlabeled test chemistry without using test targets.
backlog.title: Transductive fingerprint vocabulary

backlog.spec: Change only the tree growth policy of the existing CatBoost MAE model. Use grow_policy='Lossguide' with max_leaves=24 and min_data_in_leaf=5, and drop the fixed depth argument (Lossguide requires leaf-wise growth). Set iterations to 800 and learning_rate to 0.05 as before, and keep the OLS prior and residual target. Leaf-wise trees fit local chemistry families differently from symmetric depth-6 trees, which may help where the test scaffolds sit in sparse regions of the training data.
backlog.title: CatBoost Lossguide grow policy

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, find its k=10 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto on binary Morgan radius-2 fingerprints. Build training pairs (i, j) from training molecules and their 10 nearest training neighbours, with target d_ij = y_i - y_j and features [x_i, x_j, x_i - x_j] using the existing descriptors and fingerprints. Fit one CatBoost regressor (MAE loss, depth 6, 800 iterations) on the pairs. For a test molecule t, predict y_t as the mean over its 10 anchors j of (y_j + f(x_t, x_j, x_t - x_j)). Subsample pairs to at most 30000 for the 6 GB and 10 minute limits. This turns a regression into local analogical differences and can reduce bias on molecules in sparse regions.
backlog.title: Pairwise difference learning with nearest-neighbour anchors

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE model on the residual. First fit a CatBoost regressor with RMSE loss (depth 4, 300 iterations) on the absolute values of the first-pass in-sample residuals, using the same features, to estimate a per-molecule scale s_i (clip to the 5th and 95th percentiles, and floor at a small positive number). Then refit the main MAE CatBoost with sample_weight = 1 / s_i. The weighting down-weights molecules whose target is intrinsically noisy so the median fit concentrates on the reliable regions, and it does not change the prediction target.
backlog.title: Heteroscedastic MAE weighting from a second spread model

backlog.spec: Train a teacher as the current OLS prior plus CatBoost MAE model. Form soft training targets for each training molecule as a blend of the true label and the teacher's out-of-fold prediction: y_soft = 0.5 * y + 0.5 * oof_pred, where oof_pred comes from 4-fold inner splits grouped by Murcko scaffold within the training fold. Fit a fresh student (same OLS prior and CatBoost MAE settings, different seed) on y_soft, and predict with the student alone. The distillation step smooths labels toward out-of-fold consensus and reduces the variance of the final model on unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Self-distillation of the boosted residual model

backlog.spec: Add a hashed count fingerprint of Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pairs (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D with Generate.Gen2DFingerprint, folded to 1024 bins by modulo, counts kept) and concatenate it with the existing featurize() output. Keep the OLS prior, the CatBoost MAE residual model and all other settings unchanged. Only the fingerprint block changes.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pair counts

backlog.spec: For each molecule, compute the Murcko scaffold and its generic version (MurckoScaffold.MakeScaffoldGeneric). Build a 512-bit hashed Morgan count vector of the generic scaffold atoms and a second 512-bit count vector of side-chain environments (atoms not in the scaffold), and concatenate both to featurize(). The rest of fit_predict is unchanged. The aim is to expose ring-agnostic substituent information to CatBoost.
backlog.title: Generic-scaffold plus side-chain Morgan block

backlog.spec: Run AllChem.ComputeGasteigerCharges on each molecule and append 8 scalars: sum of positive partial charges, sum of negative partial charges, max and min atomic charge, the charge-weighted TPSA (sum over N and O atoms of |charge| times their contribution), the count of atoms with |charge| above 0.2, and the mean absolute charge. Append these to the existing feature vector. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge polar summaries

backlog.spec: Before featurisation, neutralise and canonicalise every training SMILES (Chem.MolToSmiles of the neutralised, sanitised molecule), group identical canonical strings, and replace each group with a single row whose target is the mean of the group's labels. Apply the same canonicalisation to the test SMILES for featurisation only. Everything else in fit_predict stays as it is.
backlog.title: Canonical-SMILES deduplication with label averaging

backlog.spec: Compute the Morgan count fingerprint on kekulized molecules (Chem.Kekulize with clearAromaticFlags=True) instead of aromatic ones, while keeping the RDKit descriptor block computed on the aromatic molecules. This changes only the fingerprint input so that aromatic and aliphatic ring bonds encode differently. The OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual model are unchanged.
backlog.title: Kekulized fingerprint for aromaticity-agnostic bits

backlog.spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with an L1 (median) linear model on the counts of the 110 Crippen atom types, computed with rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs or Crippen.GetAtomContribs, plus the TPSA and MolWt terms. Fit it with sklearn QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=1e-3, solver='highs') on the training fold only and use its predictions as the prior. CatBoost MAE is still fitted to the residual of that prior.
backlog.title: Crippen atom-type count linear prior

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 4-fold scaffold-grouped inner loop on the training fold to get out-of-fold predictions of the full OLS-plus-CatBoost pipeline. Fit a two-parameter affine map y ~ a + b*pred by minimising MAE (scipy.optimize.minimize on the absolute error, starting from a=0, b=1). Refit the pipeline on all training data and apply the map to the test predictions. This corrects systematic stretch or shrinkage without adding model capacity.
backlog.title: Affine recalibration of inner out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Replace the CatBoost MAE loss with an RMSE fit wrapped in an IRLS loop. Start with the RMSE model on the OLS residual, then for 4 rounds compute residuals r, set sample_weight = 1/max(|r|, 0.05), and refit CatBoost RMSE with those weights on the same features. The final test prediction is the last round's output plus the OLS prior. Use the seed for all randomness and keep iterations and depth as they are.
backlog.title: Iteratively reweighted least squares for MAE on CatBoost RMSE

backlog.spec: Build a graph per molecule (atoms as nodes with a one-hot of element, degree, aromaticity and H-count; bonds as edges with a bond-type one-hot). Run 3 rounds of fixed, random-normal (seeded) message passing in numpy: each node sums its neighbours' features through a random 16x16 matrix followed by tanh, then sum-pools each round. Concatenate the pooled 48-dim vector to the existing features. No training of the embedding is done; it is a random-feature graph embedding.
backlog.title: Untrained random-weight message-passing embedding

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make 4 jittered copies of the training descriptor block (only the RDKit descriptor columns, standardised on the training fold) by adding Gaussian noise with sd 0.1 in standardised units, keeping the original labels. Stack the copies with the original rows and fit the same CatBoost MAE residual model on the augmented set. Test features are not jittered. Seed the noise with the seed argument.
backlog.title: Gaussian descriptor-jitter augmentation

incumbent.description: Fit an OLS baseline on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP, train the existing CatBoost model on the residuals, and add the linear prediction back for test molecules (applied to the current CatBoost incumbent, since the spec's random forest is no longer in train.py).

memo: Helped: compact descriptors (MACCS 0.4096 vs 0.4417 baseline), CatBoost MAE loss (0.3837), and an OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP with CatBoost fit on residuals (0.3757 and 0.3664; incumbent mean_adjusted 0.3711). Did not help: Morgan counts (0.4451), Tanimoto kernel ridge (0.4357), MLP (0.4734), LightGBM l1 (0.3882), stacking (0.3904), PCA (0.3893), torsion counts (0.3771), 3D shape (0.3780), ElasticNet (0.3840), monotone constraints (0.3869), ionisation SMARTS (0.3764), local linear prior (0.3886), Nystroem prior (0.3915). Within noise (sd about 0.0037): residual refinements (0.3718, 0.3716), scaffold weighting (0.3724), median prior (0.3726), pruning (0.3728). Best recent: two-phase Huber then MAE boosting (0.3701), only -0.0010 vs incumbent, so likely noise. Plateau: extra features, model swaps and target tricks lose. Next: tune CatBoost depth, learning rate, iterations and l2 on the residual setup, which is untried, and seed-average CatBoost. Replicate anything near 0.37. Avoid family swaps and feature stacking.
